purpose: Three offline SAM 2.1 mask examples. Coordinates are on source images. Green points are positive, red points are negative, yellow rectangle is the box prompt.
model_choice: SAM 2.1 base: repository-recommended balance, locally available, CUDA-compatible, and does not require gated SAM 3 access.

runs.target: large foreground three_wheeler with visible driver
runs.preliminary_observation: Vehicle body and roof are covered; the negatively prompted driver is mostly excluded. Open spaces are not uniformly filled. Student must verify the full visible boundary, rider exclusion, holes, glass, and any carried/fixed items.

runs.target: foreground three_wheeler touching/overlapping another vehicle in view
runs.preliminary_observation: The foreground vehicle is isolated from the neighboring three-wheeler at the negative point. Student must inspect touching boundaries, windows/glass, seats, wheels, holes, and spill into adjacent objects.

runs.target: foreground right three_wheeler next to a standing person and other vehicles
runs.preliminary_observation: The target vehicle is covered while the negatively prompted standing person and neighboring vehicles are excluded. Student must check the windshield/glass convention, open cabin regions, small protrusions, undercarriage, and whether any visible rider exists.

review_status: Automated generation complete. The student confirmed in chat that the three overlays satisfy the requested visual/contract checks. Initial observations remain disclosed as AI-generated and student-confirmed.

student_confirmation.scope: All seven review checks listed by the assistant: boundary quality, fixed vehicle parts, person/rider exclusion, adjacent-object exclusion, glass/shadow/hole treatment, protruding cargo treatment, and independent three_wheeler class correctness.

contract_checks: Visible mask boundary should be within about 3 px; ignore finer detail than wheel/handlebar scale.
Small holes under 5% may be filled; large holes should be excluded.
Shadows are excluded; vehicle glass is included under v1.0.
Touching objects need separate non-overlapping polygons; foreground object owns the contact boundary.
Person/rider is a separate object from the vehicle.
Cargo protrusion and glass/interior treatment are still open calibration questions in v1.0.
